👄 Pronunciation Tips

TH /θ/

Tongue lightly between the teeth; no voice.

TH /ð/

Same position, but add your voice.

F / V

F has no vibration; V has vibration.

S / Z

S is unvoiced; Z uses your voice.

🎯 Minimal Pairs

ship / sheep

/ɪ/ vs /iː/

cat / cut

/æ/ vs /ʌ/

fan / van

/f/ vs /v/

rice / rise

/s/ vs /z/

right / light

/r/ vs /l/

cheap / sheep

/tʃ/ vs /ʃ/

🎤 Shadowing Lab

Listen → repeat → shadow. 20 short practice exercises.

🎤

Denzel-style practice

Beginner • Speak clearly and calmly.

“I believe I can improve every day.”
🎤

Obama-style practice

Beginner • Focus on rhythm and confidence.

“We can learn together and make progress.”
🎤

Everyday American

Beginner • Natural greeting practice.

“Hey, how are you doing today?”
🎤

Everyday American

Beginner • Short response practice.

“I'm doing well, thank you.”
🎤

Denzel-style practice

Beginner • Confident sentence stress.

“You have to keep going.”
🎤

Everyday American

Beginner • Useful classroom phrase.

“Could you say that again, please?”
🎤

Obama-style practice

Beginner • Clear public-speaking rhythm.

“Our goal is to communicate clearly.”
🎤

Everyday American

Beginner • Conversation starter.

“What are you working on today?”
🎤

Denzel-style practice

Intermediate • Emphasize key words.

“Don't let fear decide your future.”
🎤

Obama-style practice

Intermediate • Practice measured pauses.

“Progress begins when we choose to act.”
🎤

Everyday American

Intermediate • Natural explanation.

“I didn't understand the first part.”
🎤

Everyday American

Intermediate • Polite clarification.

“What exactly do you mean by that?”
🎤

Denzel-style practice

Intermediate • Strong contrast.

“It's difficult, but it isn't impossible.”
🎤

Obama-style practice

Intermediate • Motivational rhythm.

“We learn from mistakes and move forward.”
🎤

Everyday American

Intermediate • Fluent opinion.

“In my opinion, practice matters more than perfection.”
🎤

Everyday American

Intermediate • Storytelling rhythm.

“Yesterday, I met someone who changed my perspective.”
🎤

Denzel-style practice

Advanced • Emotional emphasis.

“Your circumstances do not have to define you.”
🎤

Obama-style practice

Advanced • Formal rhythm.

“Real progress requires patience, discipline, and consistency.”
🎤

Everyday American

Advanced • Natural argument.

“I understand your point, but I see the situation differently.”
🎤

Everyday American

Advanced • Nuanced opinion.

“The most useful skill is the ability to communicate under pressure.”

Practice useful conversations you can use in real life.

Alex: Hello! How are you today?
Student: I'm fine, thank you. How about you?
Alex: I'm doing great. What are you studying?
Student: I'm studying English.
Alex: Why are you learning English?
Student: Because I want to communicate with people from around the world.

🌍 English-Speaking Countries Encyclopedia

Detailed learning profiles for the 19 African and 6 Western English-speaking countries already in English With Alex.

🇨🇮

Côte d'Ivoire

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Yamoussoukro

🗣️ Languages

French; many Ivorian languages

🗺️ Geography

West African coastal country; tropical south and savanna north.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for cocoa, coffee, cashew, football, music, masks, festivals and a highly diverse population.

🇬🇧 English

English is increasingly useful for regional trade, tourism, diplomacy, technology and international study.

🎓 Student note

Students can compare French, Dioula and English vocabulary and explore how multilingualism shapes identity.

🇬🇭

Ghana

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Accra

🗣️ Languages

English; Akan, Ewe, Ga and others

🗺️ Geography

West Africa, Gulf of Guinea; forests, coast and northern savanna.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for kente, Adinkra, highlife, hiplife, festivals, cocoa and historic forts.

🇬🇧 English

English is an official language used in education, government, media and business.

🎓 Student note

Study Ghanaian English, proverbs and the history of independence under Kwame Nkrumah.

🇳🇬

Nigeria

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Abuja

🗣️ Languages

English; Hausa, Yoruba, Igbo, Nigerian Pidgin and many others

🗺️ Geography

Large West African country with rainforest, savanna, major rivers and a long Atlantic coast.

🎭 Culture & economy

Afrobeats, Nollywood, literature, fashion, food and hundreds of cultural traditions make Nigeria globally influential.

🇬🇧 English

English is central to public life, education, media and professional communication; Nigerian English has distinctive features.

🎓 Student note

Explore Achebe, Soyinka and Adichie while learning Nigerian English vocabulary.

🇰🇪

Kenya

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Nairobi

🗣️ Languages

English; Swahili and many local languages

🗺️ Geography

East African country with highlands, savanna, Indian Ocean coast and the Great Rift Valley.

🎭 Culture & economy

Famous for athletics, wildlife conservation, tea, coffee, coastal culture and Nairobi's technology scene.

🇬🇧 English

English and Swahili are official; English is prominent in education, government and business.

🎓 Student note

Compare Kenyan English with British and American varieties and study African literature.

🇺🇬

Uganda

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Kampala

🗣️ Languages

English; Swahili and many local languages

🗺️ Geography

Landlocked East African country around the Great Lakes region and source area of the Nile.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for Lake Victoria, mountain gorillas, music, dance, agriculture and diverse cultures.

🇬🇧 English

English is an official language and a major language of education and administration.

🎓 Student note

Learn vocabulary around wildlife, geography and East African society.

🇿🇦

South Africa

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Pretoria; Cape Town legislative; Bloemfontein judicial

🗣️ Languages

11 official languages including English, isiZulu and isiXhosa

🗺️ Geography

Southern African country with varied coasts, mountains, grasslands and semi-arid regions.

🎭 Culture & economy

Rich in literature, music, sport, food and history; home to diverse communities and major cities.

🇬🇧 English

English is one of the official languages and is widely used in business, education and media.

🎓 Student note

Study multilingualism, South African English and the country's complex history.

🇿🇲

Zambia

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Lusaka

🗣️ Languages

English; Bemba, Nyanja, Tonga and others

🗺️ Geography

Landlocked southern African country with high plateaus, rivers and Victoria Falls on the border region.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for Victoria Falls, wildlife, copper mining, music and warm community traditions.

🇬🇧 English

English is official and widely used in schools, government and formal communication.

🎓 Student note

Explore environmental vocabulary and tourism English.

🇿🇼

Zimbabwe

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Harare

🗣️ Languages

English; Shona, Ndebele and others

🗺️ Geography

Landlocked southern African country with highlands, savanna and major rivers.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for Great Zimbabwe, Victoria Falls region, literature, music and wildlife.

🇬🇧 English

English is an official language alongside Shona, Ndebele and other languages.

🎓 Student note

Great for studying history, archaeology and African English.

🇱🇷

Liberia

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Monrovia

🗣️ Languages

English; Liberian English and many local languages

🗺️ Geography

West African coastal country founded in the nineteenth century with strong historical ties to the United States.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for rainforest, Atlantic beaches, diverse communities and a distinctive historical identity.

🇬🇧 English

English is official; Liberian English varieties are widely spoken.

🎓 Student note

Study how migration and history influenced Liberian English.

🇸🇱

Sierra Leone

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Freetown

🗣️ Languages

English; Krio and many local languages

🗺️ Geography

West African coastal country with mountains, forests and beaches.

🎭 Culture & economy

Famous for Freetown, Krio culture, music, coastal scenery and diamond history.

🇬🇧 English

English is official; Krio is a major lingua franca.

🎓 Student note

Compare formal English with Krio expressions and study postcolonial history.

🇹🇿

Tanzania

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Dodoma

🗣️ Languages

Swahili and English; many local languages

🗺️ Geography

East African country with mainland territory and Zanzibar; includes Mount Kilimanjaro.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for Serengeti, Kilimanjaro, Zanzibar, wildlife, Swahili culture and tourism.

🇬🇧 English

English is important in higher education, tourism and international business alongside Swahili.

🎓 Student note

Study tourism English and geography vocabulary.

🇷🇼

Rwanda

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Kigali

🗣️ Languages

Kinyarwanda; English, French and Swahili

🗺️ Geography

Hilly Great Lakes country often called the land of a thousand hills.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for gorilla conservation, clean urban spaces, coffee, tea and strong post-genocide rebuilding.

🇬🇧 English

English has a significant role in education, government and international communication.

🎓 Student note

Learn about multilingual policy and development vocabulary.

🇸🇸

South Sudan

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Juba

🗣️ Languages

English; Arabic varieties and many local languages

🗺️ Geography

Young landlocked country in the Nile basin with vast wetlands and savanna.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for cultural diversity, the Sudd wetlands and strong oral traditions.

🇬🇧 English

English is the official language and is used in government and education.

🎓 Student note

Study nation-building, geography and multilingual communication.

🇧🇼

Botswana

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Gaborone

🗣️ Languages

English; Setswana

🗺️ Geography

Landlocked southern African country dominated by the Kalahari and famous for the Okavango Delta.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for wildlife, diamonds, conservation and stable institutions.

🇬🇧 English

English is official and used in government and formal education.

🎓 Student note

Explore environmental policy and conservation English.

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Port Louis

English, French, Mauritian Creole and others

Island country in the Indian Ocean with volcanic landscapes and multicultural communities.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for beaches, tourism, sugar, finance, food and cultural diversity.

🇬🇧 English

English is used in government and formal contexts; French and Creole are also widely used.

🎓 Student note

A useful case study for multilingual communication and tourism English.

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Victoria

Indian Ocean archipelago with granitic and coral islands.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for beaches, marine biodiversity, tourism and conservation.

🇬🇧 English

English is one of the official languages and important in tourism and administration.

🎓 Student note

Study environmental and hospitality English.

Africa
🏛️ Capital

Southern African country with desert landscapes, Atlantic coast and diverse ecosystems.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for the Namib Desert, wildlife, mining and dramatic landscapes.

🇬🇧 English

English is official and used in public administration and education.

🎓 Student note

Study geography, conservation and tourism vocabulary.

Africa

Maseru

Known for mountains, traditional blankets, horse riding and highland culture.

English is an official language alongside Sesotho.

🎓 Student note

Compare mountain geography vocabulary and formal English.

Africa

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for cultural ceremonies, crafts, wildlife and traditional arts.

🇬🇧 English

English is an official language and is used in education and government.

🎓 Student note

Study culture, ceremony and tourism vocabulary.

United States

America

Washington, D.C.

🎭 Culture & economy

Influential in technology, film, music, business, universities and global media.

🇬🇧 English

American English has major global influence and many regional varieties.

🎓 Student note

Practice American pronunciation, idioms and academic English.

United Kingdom

Europe

London

English; Welsh, Scottish Gaelic, Irish and others

Island state in northwestern Europe made up of England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for literature, universities, music, history, science and diverse regional cultures.

🇬🇧 English

British English has many accents and vocabulary differences across regions.

🎓 Student note

Compare British and American spelling, vocabulary and pronunciation.

Canada

America
🏛️ Capital

Ottawa

English and French; Indigenous languages

Large northern North American country with forests, lakes, mountains and Arctic regions.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for multicultural cities, hockey, natural landscapes, literature and bilingual federal institutions.

🇬🇧 English

English is one of the two federal official languages.

🎓 Student note

Useful for comparing Canadian English with American and British varieties.

Australia

Oceania
🏛️ Capital

Canberra

English widely used; many Indigenous languages and migrant languages

🗺️ Geography

Island continent with deserts, tropical north, temperate southeast and long coastlines.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for Aboriginal cultures, unique wildlife, sport, beaches, mining and cities such as Sydney and Melbourne.

🇬🇧 English

Australian English has distinctive pronunciation, slang and vocabulary.

🎓 Student note

Study accent differences and Australian expressions.

🎭 Culture & economy

Known for Māori culture, landscapes, agriculture, rugby and film production.

🇬🇧 English

Study Irish English expressions and the country's literary tradition.

📘 Grammar Lab — Tenses & 100 Irregular Verbs

Master the 12 core English tenses, then study 100 high-value irregular verbs with their French meanings.

Present SimpleI work / He works — habits, facts.
Present ContinuousI am working — action now.
Present PerfectI have worked — past linked to now.
Present Perfect ContinuousI have been working — duration until now.
Past SimpleI worked — finished past action.
Past ContinuousI was working — action in progress in the past.
Past PerfectI had worked — earlier past action.
Past Perfect ContinuousI had been working — duration before a past point.
Future SimpleI will work — prediction or decision.
Future ContinuousI will be working — action in progress in future.
Future PerfectI will have worked — completed before a future point.
Future Perfect ContinuousI will have been working — duration before a future point.

ℹ️ About English With Alex

A practical learning platform created to help students study, practise and build confidence through structured resources.

🎯 The role of the site

English With Alex is an educational platform designed to bring lessons, exercises, pronunciation, reading, listening, shadowing, music, literature and study methods together in one accessible place. Its purpose is to help learners understand their lessons, practise independently, identify mistakes and progressively become more confident and autonomous.

✍️ The author

Dioh Franck Alex is an English student at Université Alassane Ouattara de Bouaké, currently pursuing Licence 2 after completing Licence 1. He is the creator of English With Alex and develops the project as a student-oriented learning resource. His aim is to make useful educational content easier to access and to encourage students to keep learning, practising and improving.

🛠️ How the site is developed

The platform is progressively designed, tested and improved through HTML, CSS and JavaScript. New lessons, exercises, study resources and learning tools are organised according to student needs. The work focuses on clarity, accessibility, practical study and continuous improvement rather than replacing teachers or official educational programmes.
